summary: Plant maintenance domain foundation adds equipment asset registration, preventive-maintenance plan approval metadata, maintenance work-order release metadata, work-order completion metadata, and SAP PM/EAM parity-map linkage while explicitly refusing durable persistence, live EAM scheduling/runtime, IoT/SCADA ingestion, technician dispatch, spare-parts inventory mutation, procurement requisitions, accounting posting, Workflow execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain claims.
non_claims: no live enterprise asset management runtime
no spare-parts inventory mutation or reservation

findings: The slice is additive and isolates plant-maintenance domain invariants in a flat microservice crate rather than broadening Enterprise Suite into a monolith.
The API remains pure data-in/data-out with no I/O, durable state, network clients, scheduling runtime, or runtime side effects.
Independent scaling and deployment remain future adapter/runtime work; this slice only creates the pure domain foundation.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if missing equipment registration, missing plan approval, missing work-order release, invalid intervals, warranty-before-installation dates, unsafe refs, credential-shaped evidence refs, zero quantities, or spare-part over-consumption are accepted.
findings: Positive equipment-to-plan-to-work-order-to-completion flow and negative guard rails are covered.
Types map directly to equipment assets, functional locations, preventive-maintenance plans, maintenance work orders, and completion confirmations common to ERP asset-maintenance systems.

Focused plant-maintenance tests/clippy, ERP parity map tests/clippy, 31-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, JSON parse, data_class scan, quality-marker scan, and dependency-seam gate are recorded in verification.

alternatives_named: leave plant maintenance as a parity gap
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A flat domain foundation gives ERP PM/EAM parity a service-owned first write path while keeping scheduling runtime, mobile dispatch, IoT/SCADA, inventory/procurement/accounting integrations, Workflow, durable state, and cloud adapters out of scope.
rejected_reasons: Leaving PM as a gap weakens ERP parity after QM, PP, warehouse, procurement, and treasury foundations landed.
Live EAM runtime requires durable state, scheduling, technician assignment, asset telemetry, inventory and procurement seams, and operational SLO evidence beyond this slice.

findings: No credentials, external network calls, IoT/SCADA channels, inventory/procurement/accounting mutations, or Workflow dispatches are introduced.
Source and audit refs reject traversal, whitespace/control, and credential-shaped strings.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Pure string/date/quantity validation and small arithmetic only; no I/O or unbounded data access exists.

findings.summary: No database, network, filesystem, scheduler, IoT connector, mobile dispatch, or hot runtime path is introduced.

data_class_touched: FINANCIAL interval, lead time, labor, spare-part, variance, and downtime quantities
findings: SAP/Oracle/Microsoft official materials inform plant-maintenance coverage only; no exhaustive vendor parity or proprietary behavior clone is claimed.
The change is additive: one new crate/spec/catalog row and parity-map references; no migration or external resource is introduced.
Static evidence, task rows, and audit-chain rows document the change; runtime audit emission remains a non-claim.
No production user or data migration exists.
Package name follows oya-plant-maintenance-domain and flat microservice layout.
Machine-readable plant-maintenance spec and existing task ledger capture the slice without creating root markdown sprawl.
New code is isolated to microservices/plant-maintenance plus Enterprise Suite parity map references.
Clean architecture is preserved: domain crate depends only on data boundary kernel and std.
No new third-party dependencies were added; Cargo.lock changed only for the new workspace package.
specs/microservices/plant-maintenance.json parses successfully and evidence follows prior multispectrum shape.
Preventive interval validation, labor variance, spare-part consumption, and next-plan recalculation flags are deterministic arithmetic/boolean validation with no hidden state.

M1_challenge_assumption.challenge: A PM/EAM row in the parity map could remain a planned gap until runtime integration exists.
M1_challenge_assumption.resolution: The additive domain foundation is lower risk than a runtime claim and establishes a service-owned boundary for future adapters.

M2_independent_review.review_summary: Self-review found no security, architecture, or quality blockers; only known full-verify blockers are unrelated pre-existing catalog/data-class lanes.
